close_reason: Added precondition assertions to BOTH seed_object methods (MemoryBackend::seed_object at memory.rs:338 and MockBackend::seed_object at lib.rs:333). Validations: type_name must be one of the four known TYPE_NAME values (Calendar, CalendarEvent, CalendarEventNotification, ParticipantIdentity); value must be a JSON object whose id field matches the id argument. Five new regression tests at memory::seed_object_validation_tests cover all four failure paths plus a positive control. Updated one event::copy_successful_with_overrides test that was passing json!({}) as a placeholder — now passes json!({"id": "_placeholder_"}). Took option (b) from the bead (runtime validation); option (a) (generic over O: JmapObject) would change the API signature at ~13 test call sites and is a bigger reshape that could go on a future SemVer break.
description:
src/memory.rs:261-285 — seed_object signature:

    pub fn seed_object(
        &self,
        account_id: &str,
        type_name: &'static str,
        id: &str,
        value: serde_json::Value,
    )

with rustdoc:

    /// The `type_name` must match `O::TYPE_NAME` of the type being seeded
    /// (e.g. `"Calendar"`, `"CalendarEvent"`, `"CalendarEventNotification"`,
    /// `"ParticipantIdentity"`). The `value` must be a JSON object with at
    /// least an `id` field matching `id`.

Two distinct contract problems:

1. STRINGLY-TYPED KEY. `type_name: &'static str` requires the caller to
   know the exact wire-format string ("CalendarEvent", not "calendar_event",
   not "calendarevent"). The compiler accepts any &'static str. A typo
   like seed_object(..., "calendarevent", ...) compiles, runs, and
   silently inserts the object into a non-existent (lowercase) type-store
   that no method will ever read from. A misnamed type_name does NOT
   error — it succeeds and corrupts the test fixture.

   The four valid strings are exactly the JmapObject::TYPE_NAME values
   for Calendar / CalendarEvent / CalendarEventNotification /
   ParticipantIdentity. They could be a generic parameter
   `seed_object::<O: JmapObject>(&self, account_id, id, value)` that
   pulls O::TYPE_NAME at compile time, eliminating the typo class.
   Compare the canonical mail-server's seed::setup_seed_data at
   crate-jmap-mail-server/src/memory/seed.rs:228 — uses a typed
   SeedData struct, not stringly-typed keys.

2. UNCHECKED VALUE. The doc says "value must be a JSON object with at
   least an `id` field matching `id`" but line 280 just does

       inner.objects_mut(type_name, account_id).insert(Id::from(id), value);

   with no validation. A caller passing serde_json::json!(42) (not an
   object) or serde_json::json!({"id": "wrong-id"}) (mismatched id) gets
   no error. The value gets stored. Subsequent get_objects() reads the
   value back, calls O::deserialize on it, gets an error, and surfaces
   it as MemoryError("deserialize Calendar: ...") via memory.rs:417-421
   far from the original seed_object call. Stack trace points at the
   handler's get_objects path, not at the seed call that introduced
   the bad fixture.

What goes wrong for the caller: a test author writes seed_object("acc1",
"CalenderEvent", "ev1", json!({})) (typo in CalendarEvent, missing id
field). Test runs. Nothing happens — because the lookup never finds
the typo'd type-store, the value is silently dead in memory. A
parallel test that ALSO writes "CalendarEvent" sees no conflict.
Debugging is opaque.

Fix options:

  (a) Make seed_object generic: `pub fn seed_object<O: JmapObject>(&self,
      account_id: &str, id: &str, value: serde_json::Value)` — pulls
      O::TYPE_NAME via generic. Eliminates the stringly-typed footgun.

  (b) Validate the value is a JSON object and contains the expected
      `id` field. Return Result, or panic with a clear message
      ("seed_object: value must be a JSON object with `id` field
      matching `id` arg"). Either approach is better than silent
      storage of broken state.

  (c) Replace seed_object with a SeedData struct + setup_seed_data
      free function, matching the canonical mail-server seed::SeedData
      pattern.

P2 — fixture-construction footgun. Affects test ergonomics directly and
any downstream test or example that uses MemoryBackend through `memory`
feature.
title: MemoryBackend::seed_object takes stringly-typed type_name and unchecked serde_json::Value; doc preconditions never enforced
